newsitem.title: USA: Brokerage accused of charging illegal commissions.
newsitem.headline: Brokerage accused of charging illegal commissions.

text.p: Edward D. Jones & Co, a St. Louis, Mo.,-based brokerage, was accused on Thursday of illegally charging undisclosed commissions when it bought back interests in three unit investment trusts from its own customers, regulators said.
In an administrative proceeding, the Securities and Exchange Commission alleged the firm made illegal profits of about $120,000 by charging the the unlawful commissions.
The SEC alleged that the commissions came from investment trust repurchases made between 1990 and 1993.

The SEC said the firm violated what is known as Rule 22c-1 under the law that governs mutual funds, which prohibits the repurchase of unit investment trust interests at a price not based on the current net asset value of the UIT interests.
Unit investment trusts are investment vehicles carrying a fixed portfolio of income producing securities.

Also named respondents in the proceeding were Donald Walter, Steven Roberts, Ronald Gorgen and Charles Larimore, officials of the company who had compliance oversight at the time of the alleged violation.
The SEC alleged that the four officials, who are currently the principals of the firm, authorized the commissions charged.
Mary Beth Heying, company spokesperson, said: "The SEC order was a result of an innocent mistake. There was absolutely no evidence of intentional misconduct."

"Upon discovery, we returned the funds including interest to all affected customers and because of the innocent nature of the error, we believe that actions against the individuals named in the proceedings are unwarranted," she said.
The SEC said it will call a hearing to determine whether or not the allegations brought by its enforcement division are true and to determine what remedial sanctions, if any, are appropriate.
